title: Karnataka Seals KFC Outlet, Raids Upscale Hotels in Sweeping Food Safety Crackdown
excerpt: Health authorities seize 132 kg of rotten food from Bengaluru’s three-star and five-star hotels as social media complaints trigger the state’s most aggressive enforcement drive.
body:
• Karnataka health authorities deployed 30 special teams to inspect 26 three-star and five-star hotels across Bengaluru, seizing 132 kg of rotten food and 15 litres of used cooking oil.
  • A KFC outlet in Mangaluru was sealed and served notice after food safety officers found chicken stored in unhygienic conditions, while a Bengaluru lounge was shut down for rotten meat with fungus.
  • The crackdown, ordered by Karnataka Health Minister UT Khader, was triggered by a wave of social media complaints about unhygienic practices and artificial food colouring in restaurants.
  • FSSAI has separately issued show-cause notices to Nestlé India, KFC India and Flipkart after consumer complaints about worms in Maggi noodles and insects in delivered food packages.

Karnataka's food safety authorities have launched their most aggressive enforcement drive in recent memory, sealing a KFC outlet in Mangaluru, shutting down a Bengaluru rooftop lounge and raiding dozens of upscale hotels in a statewide sweep that has exposed systemic hygiene failures across the restaurant industry.

The Food Safety and Drug Administration deployed 30 special teams to inspect 26 three-star and five-star hotels across Bengaluru. Inspectors collected 35 food samples for laboratory testing and documented violations ranging from expired products still in use to fungal contamination on vegetables and failure to separate vegetarian and non-vegetarian food items.

What the Raids Found

The hotel-by-hotel seizures painted a grim picture. At Hotel Sky in UB City, officials seized 45 kg of rotten chicken and beef, 6 kg of vegetable cutlets and 15 litres of used cooking oil. Royal Chain Hotel lost 50 kg of duck meat and 5 kg of fish. Madras Kitchen, Tescon Hotel and Senchez Hotel all had food items seized or destroyed after being found unfit for consumption.

Skyee Lounge, perched on the 16th floor of the same UB City building, was shut down entirely after inspectors found all meat and beef on the premises rotten with fungus. Milk and curd discovered during the inspection had expired 10 days earlier.

"The drive was ordered after the department received multiple public complaints, many of them shared on social media, accusing several eateries of unhygienic practices and the sale of substandard food."

— ANI, citing Karnataka Health Department

KFC Under National Scrutiny

Separately, a KFC outlet in Mangaluru was sealed after food safety officers found chicken stored in unhygienic conditions. The action is part of a broader pattern of scrutiny facing the American fast-food chain in India. The FSSAI had earlier suspended the license of a KFC outlet in Tamil Nadu for using synthetic magnesium silicate, a substance used to purify reused cooking oil, and flagged severe hygiene deficiencies at a KFC outlet in Eluru, Andhra Pradesh.

At the national level, FSSAI has issued show-cause notices to KFC India, Nestlé India and Flipkart following consumer complaints that gained traction on social media. The Nestlé notice came after a consumer reported finding live insects and worms in a packet of Maggi noodles. The KFC notice cited inadequate cleanliness, poor waste management and deficient personal hygiene standards.

Social Media as Watchdog

What distinguishes the current crackdown is the role of social media in forcing regulatory action. Over the past several months, videos and posts across platforms have alleged unhygienic kitchen conditions, careless food handling and the use of artificial colours in popular dishes like gobi manchurian, kebabs and shawarma. The Karnataka food safety authority had earlier found bacteria and yeast in 8 of 17 shawarma samples collected from nine districts.

The state had previously carried out "Operation Eat Right" after reports of food poisoning and artificial colouring in food products, but the current drive represents a significant escalation in both scope and enforcement intensity.

Why It Matters for Diaspora Diners

For NRIs visiting India or keeping tabs on conditions at home, the revelations underscore persistent gaps between the dining experiences marketed by premium restaurants and the reality behind kitchen doors. The inspections also raise questions about food safety standards at India operations of global chains like KFC, which face far stricter oversight in Western markets.

In Mysuru, food safety officers separately inspected 70 hotels, restaurants and street food vendors, seizing over 30 kg of questionable food items including highly coloured peas and unlabelled food mixtures.

What Comes Next

Notices have been issued to the food business operators found in violation, and adjudication proceedings under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 are being initiated. The seized food samples have been sent for laboratory analysis, and further actions will depend on those results. FSSAI has directed the companies receiving national notices to submit detailed action-taken reports without delay.
nri_angle: The revelations raise food safety questions for NRIs visiting India and highlight gaps between marketed dining experiences and kitchen realities at premium establishments.
